text:
Alex: Heads up - saw an 8% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for one customer-cohort after last night's infra deploy. p99 token-generation latency up ~18ms for that cohort; overall throughput steady.

Morgan: rough window?

Alex: 2168000000-2168000600 ish. I grabbed a flamegraph and a couple traces. attaching minimal excerpts below.

Alex: ```
perf-trace 21680004 --route /v1/chat/stream --span=kernel_select
# top spans: kernel_select -> gpu_queue -> matmul_tiled_int8 (new) -> kv_lookup
# p99 latency: kernel_select 35ms -> matmul change added ~12ms on cold prefixes
```

Sam: did we switch a matmul kernel variant in the autoscheduler last night? I remember a rollback flag but thought it was gated.

Jess: we flipped the tiled-int8 path for g4dn-like hosts to improve steady-state throughput. the regression looks like warmup/cold-key-heavy cohorts hit the new kernel's cold-path perf.

Liam: infra traces show queueing didn't spike, but avg kernel init time +11ms for first token after a long idle (kv misses). that matches Alex's numbers.

Morgan: can we isolate whether the hit-rate dropped because of cache key churn vs prefetching rate? two orthogonal things:
- key normalization/tokenizer differences -> more distinct keys
- prefetch/cohort sampling reduced warming -> fewer warm prefixes

Alex: i diffed cache keys for a sample of requests. ~60% of the miss-set had extra tool metadata (call.metadata) appended in different orders, and ~25% looked like tokenizer whitespace differences from tokenizer v2.

Alex: example keys (sanitized):
```
sha256(system=base|tok=v1|prompt="Hello")
sha256(system=base|prompt="Hello"|tok=v1)
```
same semantic prompt, different ordering -> different key.

Jess: that's on us: a subtle change in the function-call marshalling added optional fields and we didn't canonicalize field ordering when serializing into the cache key.

Morgan: action: we should canonicalize tool/function metadata (sorted keys) and include tokenizer-version explicitly in the key. will also add a checksum of the normalized prompt instead of raw string.

Sam: +1. also propose cohort prefetch policy tweak: increase sampling alpha for low-traffic cohorts during peak warmup windows. simple experiment: alpha=0.2 -> 0.5 only for canary cohort.

Liam: infra note: increasing alpha means more prefetch traffic; we need to make sure Dedicated pools have burst headroom. I'll add a hard cap on concurrent warms per-node.

Alex: plan sketch:
1) quick revert: pin tokenizer version in cachekey generator (fast rollback string change)
2) short-term patch: stable canonicalizer for function/tool fields (sort keys, drop nulls)
3) canary: cohort prefetch alpha bump + kernel fallback policy (if kernel cold-init > 10ms for first tokens, prefer older kernel for first N tokens)
4) perf run and hit-rate eval over 24h

Morgan: can you open a PR for (1) and (2)? we want code changes small. I'll own the canary rollout and metric dashboards.

Alex: PR #: https://git.internal/r/infra/1234 (draft) - includes unit tests for field ordering and tokenizer_version tag.

Jess: small snippet of canonicalizer prototype:
```
def canonical_key(sys, prompt, tools, tok_version):
  tools_sorted = sorted((k,v) for k,v in tools.items() if v is not None)
  normalized_prompt = normalize_whitespace(prompt)
  return sha256(f"sys={sys}|tok={tok_version}|tools={json.dumps(tools_sorted)}|p={normalized_prompt}")
```

Sam: seems reasonable. want to run a small offline rekeying job on a day's traces to estimate how many keys collapse.

Alex: did a quick pass: rekeying collapsed ~72% of misses in our sample. promising.

Liam: timeline: if PRs merge today we can cut a canary tomorrow morning. infra will add node caps and a fallback rule in the routing layer.

Morgan: metrics to watch during canary:
- prefix_cache_hit_rate (cohort + global)
- p99 token latency (cohort)
- kernel_init_latency (first 10 tokens)
- prefetch traffic and warm concurrency per-node

Alex: one more gotcha - system prompt rotations. marketing pushed a system prompt tweak last week for tone. that creates a whole new set of keys if we embed system verbatim. proposal: include system prompt id/version rather than raw text in cache keys.

Jess: agreed. we'll require system_prompt_id in the call metadata and fallback to fingerprint(system_prompt_text) if id missing.

Morgan: alright. I'll own rollout + dashboard. Alex, Sam, Jess, Liam please add short runbooks for rollback (pin old kernel, restore alpha, revert canonicalizer) in the PR description.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary group "cohort-c" -> 2168003600 UTC

Alex: thanks. leaving traces and sample logs in the ticket: https://tickets.internal/INF-778

Sam: follow-up: let's add a perf test that simulates prefix-heavy traffic with tokenizers v1/v2 mix so we can catch regressions earlier in CI.

Jess: noted.

Morgan: action items summarised:
- Alex: attach full trace bundle + sample key diff
- Jess: complete canonicalizer PR + tests
- Sam: offline rekeying job + perf test
- Liam: infra caps + fallback rule
- Morgan: canary rollout + dashboards

Alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
